claims.claim: Go usually needs a few KB to tens of KB per idle connection, so 60k connections is often a few GB
claims.measured: go-gin peak memory 16 MB and go-nethttp 15 MB with 256 busy HTTP connections, against 2 MB idle
claims.why: The benchmark tops out at 256 short HTTP connections and never measures idle WebSocket connections, so it can't confirm the per-connection memory or what 60k connections would cost.

claims.claim: Reverb's per-connection cost could be much higher [than Go's]
claims.why: Reverb was not benchmarked, and the Laravel and Octane HTTP servers that were tell us nothing about Reverb's WebSocket memory per connection.

claims.claim: Node or Elixir are both good at connection-heavy work, with little benefit over Go
claims.measured: I/O wait test at 256 connections: elixir-phoenix 18,711 req/s, node-fastify 17,462, node-express 14,188, go-gin 20,235, go-nethttp 18,905
claims.why: In the high-concurrency I/O-wait test, Elixir and Node came within roughly 1.5x of Go, which fits 'good at it, but little gain over Go'.
